papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review discusses how machine learning and computational approaches can be used to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations that create epigenetic dysregulation and intratumoral heterogeneity. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, combined with computational modeling, could help uncover mechanisms of treatment resistance that remain poorly understood.

papers.title: Intra-Abdominal Sporadic Desmoid Tumors with Canonical CTNNB1 and Uncommon Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway Somatic Mutations-A Clinicopathologic and Genetic Study of Five Cases.
papers.abstract: Desmoid tumors (DTs) may be sporadic or associated with familial polyposis syndromes, including familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) and its variant, Gardner syndrome (GS). DTs are pathogenetically linked to activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. In sporadic DT, CTNNB1 is most frequently implicated, with exon 3 somatic mutations (T41A, S45F and S45P) being the most commonly reported. APC is implicated in FAP/GS-associated DTs and occasionally in sporadic DT, most often through alterations involving the exon 15 mutation cluster region. In this study of five sporadic intra-abdominal
papers.summary: This study characterizes five cases of sporadic intra-abdominal desmoid tumors, identifying canonical CTNNB1 exon 3 mutations (T41A, S45F, S45P) as well as uncommon somatic alterations in other Wnt/β-catenin pathway genes. The findings expand the known mutational spectrum of sporadic desmoid tumors beyond the classic CTNNB1 hotspots, highlighting additional pathway components that may drive tumorigenesis.

papers.title: DUET-seq: An Open-Source Droplet Platform for High-Fidelity Joint Chromatin and Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Temporal Regulatory Decoupling in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: Joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell enables direct linkage of regulatory elements to transcriptional output, but existing approaches remain limited by low co-capture sensitivity, proprietary platforms, and high costs. Here we present DUET-seq, an open-source droplet microfluidic platform for joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus. DUET-seq combines programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads with one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to physically co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments, completin
papers.summary: DUET-seq is an open-source droplet microfluidic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus by using programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads and one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods—low co-capture sensitivity, proprietary platforms, and high cost—and reveals temporal regulatory decoupling between chromatin and transcriptome in single cells.

papers.title: [Genome-wide identification, expression profiling, and natural allelic variation analysis of the ckx genes in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor)].
papers.abstract: Cytokinin (CK) is one of the essential plant hormones, and cytokinin oxidase (CKX) is the key enzyme for CK degradation. Currently, the ckx gene family of rice (Oryza sativa) and maize (Zea mays) have been characterized, while a genome-wide analysis of the ckx gene family in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) has not been reported. This study aims to identify the Sbckx gene family in sorghum, analyze its evolutionary characteristics and expression patterns, and screen for key genes. A combined approach of bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation was utilized to examine sorghum subjected to a
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study performs the first genome-wide identification and characterization of the cytokinin oxidase (ckx) gene family in sorghum, analyzing evolutionary relationships, expression patterns, and natural allelic variation. The authors combine bioinformatics with experimental validation to screen for key Sbckx genes potentially involved in cytokinin regulation. The work provides a foundation for functional studies and genetic improvement of sorghum.

papers.title: Web servers and bioinformatics tools for cancer research: A review.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of high-throughput technologies and multi-omics profiling has transformed cancer research by enabling systematic characterization of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, immunological, and pharmacological features of tumors. These diverse molecular alterations contribute to tumor initiation, progression, heterogeneity, treatment response, and resistance, creating a need for computational resources capable of integrating and interpreting complex cancer datasets. Consequently, numerous bioinformatics resources have been developed to organize, analyze, and interpret
papers.summary: This review surveys web servers and bioinformatics tools that support cancer research across multiple omics layers, including genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, immunology, and pharmacology. It highlights how these computational resources help integrate and interpret complex tumor datasets to study initiation, progression, heterogeneity, and treatment response. The paper serves as a catalog and guide for researchers selecting appropriate tools for multi-omics cancer analysis.

papers.title: Phylogeographical structure and genetic introgression in Salmonella enterica serotype Napoli: a genomic epidemiology study.
papers.abstract: Salmonella enterica serotype Napoli (S Napoli), a non-typhoidal Salmonella serotype that has been emerging in Italy, Switzerland, and France since the mid-1990s, has an unusual epidemiological profile that suggests a role for the environment in the transmission of these bacteria. The genomics of S Napoli has been inadequately characterised; we, therefore, aimed to provide a robust genomic framework for S Napoli surveillance.
papers.summary: This genomic epidemiology study characterizes the phylogeographic structure and genetic introgression of Salmonella enterica serotype Napoli, an emerging non-typhoidal serotype in Italy, Switzerland, and France since the mid-1990s. The authors provide a robust genomic framework for surveillance, revealing how environmental transmission and genetic exchange shape the spread of this pathogen.

papers.title: Ultrafast Workflow for Accurate Full-length ABO Genotyping using Nanopore Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Rapid ABO discrepancy resolution is critical for transfusion safety. However, current short-read sequencing cannot resolve phase across the 21.9 kb ABO gene. Here, the aim is to developed a nanopore-based workflow for full-length ABO genotyping. A workflow combining a long-range PCR (LR-PCR) amplicon spanning the ABO gene was generated from genomic DNA from 63 serologically discrepant donors and sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) Platform. PacBio HiFi sequencing was used as an orthogonal reference standard. Variant calling and haplotype reconstruction were performed using a uni
papers.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
papers.summary: This study develops a nanopore sequencing workflow using long-range PCR to capture the full 21.9 kb ABO gene, enabling accurate phasing of variants that short-read sequencing cannot resolve. Tested on 63 serologically discrepant blood donors with PacBio HiFi as an orthogonal reference, the workflow supports rapid ABO discrepancy resolution for transfusion safety.

papers.title: Genomic insights into non-tuberculous mycobacteria isolated from patients in a Chinese hospital.
papers.abstract: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are increasingly recognized as important opportunistic pathogens, yet the genomic basis of their antimicrobial resistance and virulence in clinical settings remains incompletely understood. We performed whole-genome sequencing on 28 clinical isolates of NTM collected from Chinese patients (primarily bronchoalveolar lavage fluid) between 2022 and 2025, combined with broth microdilution susceptibility testing and comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. The collection comprised diverse species, including Mycobacterium intracellulare, Mycobacterium chimaera, Mycob
papers.summary: This study sequenced the complete genomes of 28 non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) clinical isolates from Chinese patients, mostly from lung lavage samples, and paired this with antibiotic susceptibility testing. The analysis revealed diverse species and identified genomic features linked to drug resistance and virulence, improving understanding of how these opportunistic pathogens cause disease and resist treatment in clinical settings.

papers.title: XenoMix: Estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) DNA methylation microarray data. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for contamination in their analyses.

papers.title: ARCHER-LD: Rapid Long-Range Linkage Disequilibrium Calculations at Biobank Scale using GPU Acceleration.
papers.abstract: Linkage disequilibrium (LD) information from one's own dataset is considered optimal for downstream analyses such as statistical fine-mapping. However, the computational complexity (≈N22 computations for N variants) lead most studies to use external reference panels, such as from 1000 Genomes. To capture LD across all variant pairs in biobank-scale whole-genome sequencing (WGS) datasets with hundreds of millions of variants, new computational strategies are essential. We present a novel approach that uses multi-GPU distributed computing to compute R2 for every variant pair in a dataset. On chr
papers.summary: ARCHER-LD introduces a multi-GPU distributed computing approach to calculate pairwise linkage disequilibrium (R²) for every variant pair in biobank-scale whole-genome sequencing datasets, addressing the quadratic computational complexity that typically forces studies to rely on external reference panels like 1000 Genomes. This enables the use of dataset-specific LD information for downstream analyses such as statistical fine-mapping, which is considered optimal.

papers.title: A step forward in comprehensive nanopore-based forensic profiling of STRs, InDel, SNP and mtDNA for identity and appearance prediction.
papers.abstract: The targeted analysis of diverse DNA markers, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), insertion deletion polymorphisms (InDels) and DNA methylation levels, is central to forensic DNA phenotyping, enabling inference of BGA, appearance traits, and age. Such information is relevant when DNA comparison after conventional DNA profiling fails to identify a person of interest. Recent technological developments allow both genetic and epigenetic markers to be analyzed in long-reads within a single platform such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT). This approach offers an advantage over trad
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing can simultaneously profile multiple forensic DNA markers—STRs, InDels, SNPs, and mtDNA—along with DNA methylation, enabling both identity testing and appearance/ancestry/age prediction from a single platform. The approach offers a more comprehensive forensic profiling workflow than conventional short-read or capillary methods, though the abstract is truncated before full results are described.

papers.title: The reference shapes the signal: chrX genotype summaries and classifier sex disparity between GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 callsets.
papers.abstract: Laboratories that move from GRCh38 to T2T-CHM13 take on a new callset as well as a new assembly. I asked whether the move changes sex-chromosome genotype summaries, and whether it changes how well classifiers trained on those summaries serve males and females. I compared the published 1000 Genomes GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 callsets for 3,202 people. The two callsets come from different alignment, calling, phasing and filtering workflows, so every difference below belongs to the reference and its pipeline together. In women, the fraction of non-reference chrX genotypes that were heterozygous was 0.6
papers.summary: This study compares chrX genotype summaries between the GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 1000 Genomes callsets for 3,202 individuals, finding that the reference assembly and its associated pipeline jointly alter sex-chromosome genotype summaries. These differences in turn affect how well classifiers trained on such summaries perform for males versus females, revealing a sex disparity tied to reference choice.

papers.title: DNAharvester: A Nextflow Pipeline for Analysing Highly Degraded DNA from Ancient and Historical Specimens.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA (aDNA) research has advanced rapidly with the development of high-throughput sequencing, enabling genome-wide analyses of large collections of prehistoric specimens. However, analysing palaeontological and archaeological material with highly degraded DNA constitutes a major bioinformatic challenge. DNA from such samples is characterized by short fragment lengths, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and cross-species contamination, which can increase spurious mapping and reference bias, affecting downstream population genetic inferences.
papers.summary: DNAharvester is a Nextflow pipeline designed to process highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens, addressing challenges like short fragments, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and contamination. It aims to reduce spurious mapping and reference bias, improving the reliability of downstream population genetic analyses for aDNA studies.

papers.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validat
papers.summary: This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5hmC profiling add useful information beyond standard mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies, where plasma variant interpretation is confounded by clonal hematopoiesis and treatment-related changes. The authors find that direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies remain retrospective and internally validated, limiting clinical translation.

papers.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network.
papers.abstract: Somatic mosaicism is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of human biology, yet the detection of somatic mutations remains challenging. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network conducted large-scale benchmarking experiments involving cell lines and donor tissues to evaluate sequencing technologies, experimental approaches, and computational methods for detecting different types of somatic mutations, generating community resources with >1,000× short-read and 100-400× long-read data for nine analyzed samples. We determined effective strategies for utilizing short- a
papers.summary: The SMaHT Network benchmarked sequencing technologies and computational methods for detecting somatic mutations using cell lines and donor tissues, generating community resources with over 1,000× short-read and 100-400× long-read coverage across nine samples. The study identifies effective strategies for combining short- and long-read data to detect different classes of somatic mutations, providing a reference framework for the field.

papers.title: Fast3VmrMLM enables statistically powerful and computationally efficient large-scale marker-pair epistasis GWAS in sizable populations.
papers.abstract: Identifying marker-pair epistasis in genome-wide association studies remains challenging due to computational burden and statistically underpowered. Hence, we developed a big-data algorithm, Fast3VmrMLM, that integrates a genome-wide pairwise scanning plus machine-learning framework with seven big-data techniques. Fast3VmrMLM considers all possible genetic effects while controlling for all polygenic backgrounds, substantially improving power of identifying epistasis. To broaden its utility, we extended three modules: Fast3VmrMLM-Hap for haplotype-by-haplotype interactions, Fast3VmrMLM-NCII for
papers.summary: Fast3VmrMLM is a new big-data algorithm for detecting marker-pair epistasis in genome-wide association studies that combines genome-wide pairwise scanning with machine learning and seven big-data techniques to overcome computational and statistical power limitations. It accounts for all possible genetic effects while controlling for polygenic backgrounds, substantially improving power to identify epistatic interactions. The authors also extended it with modules for haplotype-by-haplotype interactions (Fast3VmrMLM-Hap) and other analyses (Fast3VmrMLM-NCII).

papers.title: Integration of Collaborative Cross and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel studies does not significantly improve genome wide association study results.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies rely on maximizing cohort size and minimizing environmental noise to increase their efficacy. Model organism Genetic Reference Populations offer significantly reduced environmental noise and deep phenotyping, yet rarely are multiple populations merged together. We evaluated whether combining the Collaborative Cross (CC) and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel (HMDP), two well-studied murine Genetic Reference Populations would improve GWAS outcomes. Utilizing two prior studies by our group that had performed the same study for heart failure in each cohort, we examined e
papers.summary: This study tested whether combining two mouse genetic reference populations, the Collaborative Cross and the Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel, improves genome-wide association study power for heart failure traits. Using data from prior studies of the same phenotype in each cohort, the authors found that merging the populations did not significantly improve GWAS results, likely due to differences in population structure and genetic architecture.

papers.title: FAMUS: A Few-Shot Learning Framework for Large-Scale Protein Annotation.
papers.abstract: Gene function prediction is pivotal in genomic and metagenomic data analysis. Current annotation tools typically rely on the most similar sequence from the query database and struggle to robustly set meaningful hit thresholds, causing a major challenge for reliable annotation.
papers.summary: FAMUS introduces a few-shot learning framework for large-scale protein function annotation that moves beyond the common practice of relying on the single most similar sequence and manually tuned hit thresholds. By learning from a small number of labeled examples, it aims to provide more robust and reliable gene function predictions for genomic and metagenomic data.

papers.title: "A human CHRNA6 3' UTR variant alters the molecular environment and microRNA engagement of the adolescent VTA without changing Chrna6 transcript abundance".
papers.abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6 , encoding the α6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the "C" or "G" allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how a common non-coding variant (rs2304297) in the 3' UTR of the CHRNA6 gene, linked to adolescent smoking, exerts its effects. Using humanized rats, the authors show that the variant does not change Chrna6 transcript levels or stability, but instead alters the local molecular environment and microRNA binding in the adolescent ventral tegmental area, suggesting a post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism.

papers.title: Structural and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Human β-Defensin 1 Variants Reveals Distinct Perturbation Signatures.
papers.abstract: Human β-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze how naturally occurring genetic variants in human β-defensin 1 (hBD-1), an antimicrobial peptide important for epithelial innate immunity, affect the protein's structure and dynamics. The authors identify distinct perturbation signatures for different variants, suggesting molecular mechanisms by which coding substitutions could alter hBD-1 function and infection susceptibility. The work links genomic variation to structural consequences in a small disulfide-constrained peptide.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of incomplete penetrance in 4,325 rare disease families reveals divergent transcriptional networks in CHD8 pathology.
papers.abstract: Despite major advances in genomic sequencing and analytical pipelines for rare disorders, more than 50% of affected individuals remain without a molecular diagnosis. One challenge is the interpretation of inherited variants exhibiting incomplete penetrance (IP).
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint systematically evaluates incomplete penetrance across 4,325 rare disease families, addressing a major barrier to molecular diagnosis in rare disorders. Using CHD8 pathology as a case study, the authors identify divergent transcriptional networks that may explain why some carriers of pathogenic variants remain unaffected. The work highlights how network-level analysis can help interpret inherited variants with incomplete penetrance.

papers.title: Beyond molecular snapshots: Regulatory trajectories in dynamic epigenetic regulation.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation is commonly interpreted through molecular markers measured at discrete timepoints. While such approaches have generated important biological insights, they primarily provide static representations of regulatory states and may therefore capture only a limited component of dynamic biological processes. Emerging evidence from chromatin biology, transcriptional regulation and genome organisation suggests that biological regulation unfolds through continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers. This article presents a biological hypothesis and conceptual f
papers.summary: This conceptual article argues that epigenetic regulation is fundamentally dynamic and poorly captured by static molecular snapshots at discrete timepoints. The authors propose a hypothesis that regulation unfolds through continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers, including chromatin, transcription, and genome organization, and call for trajectory-based frameworks to study it.

papers.title: Overcoming a diagnostic blindspot: Identifying balanced translocations in Mendelian rare disease cohorts.
papers.abstract: Short-read genome sequencing generates the signal necessary to detect balanced reciprocal translocations at single-nucleotide resolution, but standard structural variant callers represent them as breakend pairs. Structural variant callers produce thousands of breakend records per genome, the majority of which are false positives arising from segmental duplications, repetitive elements, and reference assembly artifacts. This specificity problem has prevented balanced translocation detection from entering routine genome sequencing workflows. We developed a highly specific pipeline to resolve bal
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a highly specific computational pipeline to detect balanced reciprocal translocations from short-read genome sequencing data, addressing the problem that standard structural variant callers produce thousands of false-positive breakend records. This enables balanced translocation detection to enter routine genome sequencing workflows for Mendelian rare disease cohorts, where such variants are a known diagnostic blind spot.

papers.title: Ryder: epigenome normalization using a two-tier model and internal reference regions.
papers.abstract: Sequencing-based epigenomic profiling methods are powerful but suffer from technical variability that complicates cross-sample comparisons and can obscure true biological signals. While existing normalization methods using spike-in controls or computational approaches have been proposed, they often rely on assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions or require additional data types.
papers.summary: Ryder introduces a two-tier normalization model for sequencing-based epigenomic data that uses internal reference regions instead of spike-in controls, aiming to remove technical variability and enable more reliable cross-sample comparisons. This computational approach avoids assumptions that often fail across diverse experimental conditions and does not require additional data types.

papers.title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including Mini-Mental State
papers.summary: The authors present HINN, a deep learning framework that encodes biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships when predicting cognitive assessment scores from blood-derived multi-omics data. The approach aims to improve interpretability and biomarker prioritization by constraining the network architecture with prior biological knowledge rather than treating omics layers as unstructured inputs.

papers.title: A clinical case of X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia caused by an Xq13.1 duplication affecting the EDA gene.
papers.abstract: X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED; Christ-Siemens-Touraine syndrome, ICD-10: Q82.4) is the most common type of ectodermal dysplasia, caused by genetic disorders of ectodermal derivatives. The condition significantly impacts patients' quality of life, presenting with a classic triad of hypohidrosis, hypotrichosis and hypodontia, which creates a risk of impaired thermoregulation and necessitates complex dental rehabilitation. The molecular basis of the disease lies in alterations of the EDA gene, which encodes ectodysplasin A. This protein belongs to the tumor necrosis factor (TN
papers.summary: This clinical case report describes a patient with X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia caused by an Xq13.1 duplication that affects the EDA gene, rather than the more typical point mutations. The finding expands the known mutational spectrum for this disorder and highlights the importance of copy-number analysis in diagnosing XLHED when standard sequencing is uninformative.

papers.title: Assembly-graph-assisted haplotype-resolved scaffolding of polyploid genomes.
papers.abstract: Assembling polyploid genomes at the chromosome level remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of accurately distinguishing homologous chromosomes, leaving a vast number of polyploid species without high-quality genome sequences. Current chromatin conformation capture (3C)-based haplotype-resolved scaffolding methods often produce highly incomplete and mis-phased assemblies of complex polyploids, as short sequences lacking sufficient interaction support and collapsed regions with misleading signals are difficult to resolve. Here we present GPhase, a haplotype-resolved scaffolding algorit
papers.summary: GPhase is a new algorithm for assembling chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved genomes of polyploid species. It uses assembly-graph information to overcome the limitations of 3C-based scaffolding, which often produces incomplete or mis-phased assemblies in complex polyploids. This addresses a major gap, as most polyploid species lack high-quality reference genomes.

papers.title: Interpretable neural networks prioritize cancer driver genes from genome-wide dependency landscapes.
papers.abstract: Identifying cancer driver genes and their therapeutic impact remains a core challenge in computational cancer biology. We introduce xNNDriver and xAEDriver, two interpretable neural network frameworks that connect cancer mutations with genome-wide DepMap gene dependencies, pathway activity, and drug-response patterns. xNNDriver is a supervised pathway-guided model that evaluates whether a gene's mutation status is encoded in the genome-wide dependency landscape; we interpret model fitness as a driver potential score, which quantifies the strength of this mutation-dependency signal and prioriti
papers.summary: The authors present xNNDriver and xAEDriver, two interpretable neural network frameworks that link cancer mutations to genome-wide DepMap gene dependencies, pathway activity, and drug-response patterns. xNNDriver is a supervised, pathway-guided model that scores a gene's 'driver potential' by testing whether its mutation status is encoded in the dependency landscape. This provides a way to prioritize candidate cancer driver genes from dependency data.

papers.title: Analytical and clinical validation of the EdenDx methylation assay as a noninvasive supportive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer in cervical scraping specimens.
papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy; however, early detection remains challenging due to overlapping symptoms and the absence of validated noninvasive triage testing. Diagnosis relies on invasive procedures such as endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage. The EdenDx assay detects hypermethylation of CDO1 and CELF4 genes, which are specifically associated with EC and have been shown to be epigenetically altered prior to symptom onset. Here, we evaluate the clinical and analytical performance of the EdenDx assay as a noninvasive triage tool for the early detect
papers.summary: This study validates the EdenDx assay, a noninvasive test that detects hypermethylation of the CDO1 and CELF4 genes in cervical scraping specimens to triage women for endometrial cancer. The assay aims to reduce reliance on invasive endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage by identifying early-stage disease, since these epigenetic changes appear before symptom onset. The authors report analytical and clinical performance metrics supporting its use as a supportive triage tool.

papers.title: A Guide to Enzymatic Targeted Methylation Sequencing Bioinformatics Workflow: Best Practices.
papers.abstract: We present a best-practices protocol for targeted DNA methylation sequencing analysis that integrates both bisulfite- and enzymatic-conversion approaches using Twist Bioscience technology. Building on established tools and vendor-recommended workflows, this protocol provides a standardized, fully reproducible framework that addresses current gaps in the implementation, documentation, and downstream integration of targeted methylation sequencing analyses. The workflow incorporates widely used open-source tools across two main stages: preprocessing (adapter trimming with Trim Galore and quality
papers.summary: This protocol provides a standardized, reproducible bioinformatics workflow for analyzing targeted DNA methylation sequencing data generated by both bisulfite and enzymatic conversion methods, using Twist Bioscience capture technology. It integrates open-source tools for preprocessing (e.g., adapter trimming with Trim Galore) and downstream analysis, addressing gaps in implementation and documentation. The guide aims to help researchers consistently process and interpret targeted methylation data.

papers.title: Epigenetics in cancer: from mechanisms to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Epigenetics encompasses heritable yet reversible changes in gene expression that occur without alterations to the underlying DNA sequence. Through coordinated regulation of DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization, epigenetic mechanisms shape chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs that govern cellular identity, plasticity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, disruption of the epigenetic landscape has emerged as a hallmark of tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Unlike gen
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how epigenetic mechanisms—DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization—are disrupted in cancer and contribute to tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. It frames these epigenetic alterations as a hallmark of cancer and discusses how they might be leveraged for precision medicine approaches. As a review, it consolidates mechanistic understanding and translational opportunities rather than presenting new primary data.

papers.title: DeCTCF: Decoding CTCF binding sequences by leveraging predicted epigenomic features.
papers.abstract: CTCF is a key architectural protein with diverse roles in genome organization and gene regulation, yet how it achieves these roles in different contexts remains unclear. Pretrained sequence-based models such as Sei provide predicted epigenomic features that can be used in downstream analyses of regulatory elements. Here, we developed DeCTCF, an integrative computational framework that uses pretrained Sei predictions to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences by integrating CTCF ChIP-seq data from 118 human cell lines. By leveraging predicted epigenomic features from the Sei model, we grouped th
papers.summary: DeCTCF is a computational framework that uses epigenomic features predicted by the pretrained Sei model to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences across 118 human cell lines. By integrating these predicted features with CTCF ChIP-seq data, the authors group and characterize binding sites, revealing how CTCF's diverse architectural and regulatory roles vary across cellular contexts.

papers.title: Clinical Epigenomics in Rare Diseases: Interpreting DNA Methylation Episignatures.
papers.abstract: Epigenomic testing complements sequence-based analysis by detecting downstream changes in epigenomic state associated with genetic variation. Genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures are reproducible molecular phenotypes that can serve as biomarkers of specific Mendelian disorders, particularly those involving chromatin regulators, DNA methylation machinery, and transcriptional regulatory pathways.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures—reproducible patterns of methylation change—can serve as clinical biomarkers for rare Mendelian disorders, especially those caused by mutations in chromatin regulators and DNA methylation machinery. It frames epigenomic testing as a complement to sequence-based diagnostics, helping interpret genetic variants whose downstream effects are not obvious from DNA sequence alone.

papers.title: Establishment of Uveal Melanoma Patient-Derived Organoids Using an Air-Liquid Interface System for Translational Research.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, with a unique genetic and epigenetic profile and a high metastatic risk. The lack of experimental models to replicate tumor biology, including its epigenetic landscape, limits progress in translational research. Recently, patient-derived organoid (PDO) models have emerged as a promising tool for the modeling of various tumors, including UM. This study aims to establish an air-liquid interface (ALI) PDO culture system for UM, evaluate its similarity to the primary tumors, and assess its utility for drug screening.
papers.summary: This study establishes patient-derived organoid models of uveal melanoma using an air-liquid interface culture system, aiming to better replicate the tumor's genetic and epigenetic features than existing models. The authors evaluate how closely these organoids resemble the primary tumors and test their usefulness for drug screening, addressing a key gap in translational research for this aggressive eye cancer.

papers.title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
papers.abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon
papers.summary: The authors developed ChromAgeNet, a convolutional neural network that predicts hematopoietic stem cell aging from 3D chromatin images. The model learns spatial features of chromatin architecture that change with age, providing an interpretable quantitative marker of aging. This demonstrates that chromatin organization can serve as a rich, learnable signature of the aging process.

papers.title: Investigation of allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids reveals the association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high expression in citrus genomes.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a central role in the regulation of gene expression. In plants, methylation occurs in the CG, CHG, and CHH contexts, via distinct DNA methyltransferases including MET1, CMT3, and the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway via DRM2. In interspecific hybrids, these epigenetic mechanisms are confronted to a mixed small RNA population and two subgenomes harbouring specific methylation patterns, therefore generating unique expression profiles. The aim of this work was to understand these regulations by analysing gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNAs in a citrus
papers.summary: This study examines allele-specific expression in citrus interspecific hybrids, integrating gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNA data to understand how parental subgenomes are regulated. The authors report an association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation (via the RdDM pathway) and high expression of certain alleles in citrus genomes, suggesting that small RNA-directed methylation can be linked to transcriptional activation rather than only silencing in this hybrid context.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers used to diagnose and classify central nervous system tumors, highlighting the shift from purely histology-based diagnosis to an integrated molecular framework. It emphasizes DNA methylation profiling as a key tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, alongside genomic biomarkers with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance across major CNS tumor categories.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1 patient variant R5179H, corresp
papers.summary: The authors used CRISPR-Cas9 to create a mouse model carrying the R5179H missense variant in KMT2D, a mutation found in some Kabuki syndrome type 1 patients. This complements existing loss-of-function models by allowing study of missense variants, which account for 15-30% of KS1 cases, and enables comparison of phenotypic features between variant types.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review argues that spatial transcriptomics, while valuable, captures only part of the picture, and that spatial epigenomic profiling is needed to understand how chromatin and regulatory programs are organized within intact tumor tissue. It surveys how spatial biology approaches can reveal microenvironmental organization, tumor heterogeneity, and cell-cell communication in cancer, and highlights the gap left by methods that disrupt tissue architecture.

papers.title: A Pan-Methylome Framework for Population-Scale Bacterial Epigenomics.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic modifications furnish a hidden regulatory layer that shapes cellular fate and evolutionary potential without rewriting the genetic code. In eukaryotes, methylome maps have profoundly transformed our understanding of development, disease, and lineage diversification. In bacteria, which represent the most abundant and ecologically versatile forms of life, the epigenome remains a largely uncharted dimension. To enable population-scale comparison of bacterial methylomes, we develop a principled strategy to prioritize methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded, broadly conserved
papers.summary: The authors present a framework for comparing bacterial methylomes at population scale, prioritizing methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded and broadly conserved. This addresses the current gap in bacterial epigenomics, where methylome maps remain largely uncharted compared to eukaryotes, and enables systematic population-level comparisons of bacterial epigenetic modifications.

papers.title: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling: Technologies, computation, and applications in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Cancer is an intrinsically heterogeneous disease characterized by distinct malignant subclones defined by specific genetic and epigenetic alterations, such as aberrant DNA methylation. Traditional bulk sequencing methods analyze large populations of cells in aggregate, yielding an averaged methylome signal that masks the rare but clinically significant epigenetic patterns driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. The emergence of single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing has driven a paradigm shift in oncology by providing the resolution required to dissect this
papers.summary: This review surveys single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing technologies, computational methods, and applications in precision oncology. It argues that bulk methylome profiling averages away rare, clinically important epigenetic subclones, whereas scDNAme resolves heterogeneity driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Epigenetics and In Silico Transcriptome Analysis of Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
papers.abstract: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous hematologic malignancy that accounts for about 15%-20% of childhood leukemias. Despite therapeutic advances, relapses remain common, and survival for high-risk patients is below 60%. Unlike adult AML, pediatric AML displays distinct genetic mutations, including FLT3-ITD, NPM1, KMT2A rearrangements, and core-binding factors (CBF) fusions, as well as extensive epigenetic dysregulation. Aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, and altered non-coding RNA expressions disrupt hematopoietic differentiation and activate oncogenic transc
papers.summary: This review examines how epigenetic dysregulation—including aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA changes—contributes to pediatric acute myeloid leukemia, a distinct disease from adult AML with its own mutation profile (FLT3-ITD, NPM1, KMT2A rearrangements, CBF fusions). The authors also discuss in silico transcriptome analysis approaches for studying these epigenetic and expression changes in childhood AML.

papers.title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome.
papers.abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of bialle
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning classifier that uses rare coding-region variants to distinguish familial from sporadic Meniere disease cases, achieving a test AUC of 0.843 and 81.5% accuracy with a gradient boosting model. Reclassifying 16.6–28.3% of sporadic cases as familial suggests that some sporadic diagnoses may actually carry a hidden genetic burden, including biallelic heterozygous variants.

papers.title: Data-Driven Virus Discovery with Virushunter and Virusgatherer.
papers.abstract: We present Virushunter and Virusgatherer, a bipartite computational workflow for discovering viral genomes from unprocessed next-generation sequencing data. Virushunter conducts a profile Hidden Markov Model-based sequence homology search for viral hallmark protein-coding sequence reads to construct microcontigs, which are used as seeds for targeted viral genome assembly by Virusgatherer. We showcase the application of Virushunter and Virusgatherer through an RNA virus-wide screen in 3348 bat transcriptome sequencing experiments from the Sequence Read Archive. Many of the discovered viruses ar
papers.summary: The authors present Virushunter and Virusgatherer, a two-step computational pipeline for discovering viral genomes directly from raw next-generation sequencing data. Virushunter uses profile Hidden Markov Models to identify viral hallmark protein-coding reads and assemble them into microcontigs, which Virusgatherer then uses as seeds for targeted viral genome assembly. They demonstrate the workflow by screening 3,348 bat transcriptome experiments from the Sequence Read Archive, uncovering many previously unknown RNA viruses.

papers.title: Diverse patterns of transcriptional regulation and epigenetic reprogramming within PMDs contribute to ESCC progression by regulating EMT and immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four disti
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline to map partially methylated domains (PMDs) across cancers and applied it to esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, classifying PMDs into four distinct subtypes based on gene expression. These PMD subtypes appear to regulate epithelial-mesenchymal transition and immune suppression, linking epigenetic reprogramming to tumor progression.

papers.title: Controlling for DNA dosage with whole-genome sequencing improves ATAC-seq peak calling.
papers.abstract: ATAC-seq is a powerful method for mapping chromatin accessibility and identifying cis-regulatory elements (CREs) across cell types. We reveal that ATAC-seq peak calling is compromised by local biases in DNA dosage, arising from copy number variations but also from DNA replication timing. As part of the FANTOM consortium's efforts, we propose enhancing the model-based analysis of ChIP-seq pipeline by integrating whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, analogous to input controls in ChIP-seq analyses. This adjustment increases both the number and width of ATAC peaks, with improved proximity to trans
papers.summary: ATAC-seq peak calling is biased by local variations in DNA copy number and replication timing, which can create false or distorted chromatin accessibility signals. The authors show that incorporating whole-genome sequencing data as an input control, similar to ChIP-seq input controls, improves peak calling by increasing both the number and width of detected ATAC peaks and bringing them closer to true regulatory elements. This provides a simple methodological fix for a widespread confounder in chromatin accessibility studies.

papers.title: PoLoCo: a reproducible pooled low-coverage workflow for draft genome assembly and allele frequency analysis from ethanol-preserved small non-model invertebrates.
papers.abstract: Many ecologically important small invertebrates are preserved in ethanol, which compromises DNA integrity and severely limits their potential to be utilized in further genomic research. The lack of soil arthropod representation ultimately results in limited availability of reference genomes and population genomic inference from pooled sequencing (Pool-seq).
papers.summary: PoLoCo is a reproducible workflow for generating draft genome assemblies and allele frequency estimates from pooled, low-coverage sequencing of small non-model invertebrates preserved in ethanol. It addresses the challenge of degraded DNA in ethanol-preserved soil arthropods, a group poorly represented in reference genome databases, enabling population genomic inference where it was previously difficult.

papers.title: Discovery and annotation of putative genes and novel RNA splice-isoforms in the human heart.
papers.abstract: The analysis of long-read RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data can extend current annotations across the genomes, transcriptomes, and proteomes of even the most annotated species such as Homo sapiens. Long-read sequencing (LRS) technologies like Oxford Nanopore Technologies' (ONTs) nanopore sequencing can capture full-length transcripts, making the task of read-to-isoform assignment less challenging. This enables both the discovery of new RNA splice isoforms as well as a more accurate measure of their individual expression. RNA expression from unannotated regions of the genome can also lead to the di
papers.summary: Using Oxford Nanopore long-read RNA sequencing of human heart tissue, the authors identified previously unannotated genes and novel RNA splice isoforms, improving the annotation of the cardiac transcriptome. The full-length transcript reads allowed more reliable assignment of reads to specific isoforms and quantification of their expression, including transcripts from unannotated genomic regions.

papers.title: TorchGWAS 1.0: GPU-accelerated GWAS at scale.
papers.abstract: Imaging, molecular and machine-learning workflows can generate thousands of quantitative phenotypes in one cohort. Repeating genome-wide scans trait by trait creates a computational and output bottleneck.
papers.summary: TorchGWAS 1.0 introduces a GPU-accelerated framework for genome-wide association studies that can efficiently handle thousands of quantitative phenotypes from a single cohort. By leveraging GPU parallelism, it addresses the computational and output bottlenecks of running separate GWAS scans for each trait, enabling large-scale phenome-wide analyses. The tool is designed to integrate with modern imaging, molecular, and machine-learning pipelines that generate high-dimensional phenotype data.

papers.title: OBLX: building standardized reference resources for reproducible bioinformatics data analysis.
papers.abstract: Reproducible next-generation sequencing (NGS) analyses in cancer research require standardized reference genome resources, yet these resources are often assembled inconsistently, limiting the comparability of results across pipelines and studies. While existing solutions support a range of workflows, they provide only limited documentation of the included data and processing steps. Furthermore, some of these resources are not version-matched or outdated, making them less suitable for integrated and reproducible cancer genomics analyses. To address this gap, we developed the Omics builder for B
papers.summary: OBLX is a tool for building standardized, well-documented reference genome resources for reproducible NGS analysis in cancer research. It addresses the problem of inconsistently assembled and poorly documented reference resources that limit comparability across pipelines and studies. The tool aims to provide version-matched, up-to-date resources with clear documentation of included data and processing steps.

papers.title: dbcan-nf: a Nextflow pipeline for accurate CAZyme annotation in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) are crucial for carbohydrate degradation in any ecological environment. However, CAZyme annotation is not easy in whole-genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomes, due to the lack of accurate, scalable, robust, and reproducible workflows. We previously published dbCAN as a web server and associated standalone tool run_dbcan that performs CAZyme annotation with assembled genomes as the input but not with raw WGS reads.
papers.summary: dbcan-nf is a Nextflow pipeline that enables accurate and scalable annotation of carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) directly from raw whole-genome shotgun metagenomic reads, addressing a gap in the existing dbCAN web server and run_dbcan tool which required assembled genomes. The pipeline provides a reproducible, robust workflow for CAZyme annotation in metagenomes, which is important for studying carbohydrate degradation across ecological environments.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing Unravels Virulence and Antimicrobial Resistance Landscapes of Major Bovine Respiratory Disease Pathogens.
papers.abstract: Bovine respiratory diseases are a seasonally highly prevalent infectious condition and cause great economic losses to the farming industry. In order to expand the genomic database information of bovine respiratory disease pathogens, the raw data were assembled and genome annotated using relevant bioinformatics analysis software to clarify the strain virulence, resistance gene carriage, and evolution of bovine-origin Pasteurella multocida, Mannheimia haemolytica, and Mycoplasma bovis. Whole genome sequencing of Pasteurella multocida (Pm1), Mannheimia haemolytica (Mh1), and Mycoplasma bovis (Mb1
papers.summary: The authors sequenced and annotated the complete genomes of three major bovine respiratory disease pathogens—Pasteurella multocida, Mannheimia haemolytica, and Mycoplasma bovis—to characterize their virulence factors, antimicrobial resistance genes, and evolutionary relationships. This expands the genomic reference data available for these economically important veterinary pathogens.

papers.title: Characteristics of predicated pathogenic missense variants in human genes for Mendelian disorders.
papers.abstract: Missense variants represent a major class of genetic variation and contribute substantially to the cause of Mendelian disorders. However, the genetic and protein properties governing their pathogenicity remain incompletely characterized. Existing variant pathogenicity databases, such as ClinVar, are enriched for variants in well-studied genes and therefore may not provide a representative view of pathogenic missense variants across the genome. Meanwhile, recent advances in computational pathogenicity prediction have significantly improved their predictive accuracy, enabling large-scale genome-
papers.summary: This study characterizes genetic and protein-level properties that distinguish predicted pathogenic missense variants from benign ones across human genes linked to Mendelian disorders, using computational pathogenicity predictions to overcome the sampling bias of databases like ClinVar. It identifies features associated with pathogenicity that may be more representative of the genome-wide landscape than curated variant sets.

papers.title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies a missense variant in the cytoskeletal gene SVIL implicating actin remodeling in COVID-19 severity in a Pakistani cohort.
papers.abstract: The current study investigated host genetic associations with disease severity in COVID-19 patients of South Asian origin and explored its molecular basis.
papers.summary: This study performed whole-exome sequencing on a Pakistani cohort to identify host genetic variants associated with COVID-19 severity, finding a missense variant in the cytoskeletal gene SVIL. The finding implicates actin remodeling pathways in COVID-19 pathogenesis and highlights the value of studying diverse populations for host genetics of infectious disease.
